Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8166669
Permit API: 081-21757
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Gamble Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/29/2023
Comments: On November 29, 2023, DEP representatives Brad Kline, Erica Lutz, and Evan Buck conducted a incident inspection at the Inflection Energy Reynolds Well Pad. Gregg Saunders with Inflection Energy reported on November 28, 2023 that a spill from a separator onsite occurred misting production fluid onto the well pad surface. A valve body on the separator failed and spilled approximately 10 gallons of production fluid onto the well pad surface. Penn E and R was onsite for Inflection and delineated the area of impact. Inflection contractors were using a high vacuum truck to remove some of the impacted area and excavating the remainder of the area where the vacuum truck was not able to handle. The area of impact was about 30 feet by 10 feet. The depth of the excavation ranged from an inch to a foot. Excavation of the area of impact was not complete by the time DEP left the site. Soil conductivity was screened with a soil conductivity meter and ranged from 200 uS/cm to an over range reading on the meter. The upper conductivity limit of the DEP soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. The lower range measurement was from an area that the impacted soil had been removed.The spill of production fluid outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management 301.

Violation ID: 924679

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2021
Comments: On July 27, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Harmon Creek Well A 11323 Well Site in Smith Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of fluid reported by the Operator to the Department on 7/26/2021 at 16:00. The Operator reported that approximately 1.5 barrels of production water and condensate was released to the well pad due to a sight glass o-ring failure on the Gas Production Unit (GPU). At the time of inspection, the Operator was in the process of the removing the GPUs from the area impacted by the release. I observed a petroleum odor and dark staining under the middle GPU and excavated channels on either side of the middle GPU. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 30’ x 10’ in size. The staining was visible approximately 12" in depth. I spoke with Range Resources representative Nick Reda. Mr. Reda indicated that the released material was proximity 51% production water and 49% condensate oil and that the Range intends to utilize Act 2 for cleanup. No waterways were impacted by the release and no apparent migration of the material was observed. Two roll off waste disposal boxes were on site to collect the impacted material for disposal. The Operator is in compliance with the current Department spill policy for reporting the release. Violations area being issued for the release.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-09-03 to Rockdale Marcellus Llc in Union Twp, Tioga county. 78a64a(d) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT - Secondary containment failed to have storage capacity sufficient to hold the volume of the largest single aboveground primary containment, plus an additional 10% of volume for precipitation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-03
Violation Code: 78a64a(d) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT - Secondary containment failed to have storage capacity sufficient to hold the volume of the largest single aboveground primary containment, plus an additional 10% of volume for precipitation.
Violation ID: 860696
Permit API: 117-22060
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Union Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-09-03
Comments: Results from sample IDs 0718-101, 0718-102, and 0718-103, collected 8/19/2019 as documented in inspection report number 2922630, were received from the laboratory on 8/31/2019. At the time of inspection, a large volume of fluid was observed in the northeast corner of the pad surface and was discharging into the rock-lined stormwater channel, which begins at this corner of the pad, and flowing into the northeast infiltration basin. Conductivity of the fluid on the pad surface in the northeast corner of the pad had electrical conductivity (EC) readings between 4.61 mS/cm and 7.19 mS/cm. In the basin, the fluid entering from the channel had an EC of 5.85 mS/cm. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in samples 0718-101 and 0718-102, collected from the pad surface and the northeast infiltration basin, respectively, indicate that a discharge of a pollutional substance occurred. The discharge of a pollutional substance to the infiltration basin, considered Waters of the Commonwealth, is a violation of Section 401 of the Clean Streams Law. The volume of the release is underdetermined. The Department recommends following the process outlined in 78a66 in order to remediate the release. Violations noted. The violation cited on 8/26/2019 (IR #2925622) remains outstanding.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 966780
Permit API: 129-24375
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/26/2022
Comments: On August 26, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Janoscrat 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection CEI inspection in response to violations issued under inspection 3400883 where violations were issued due to a possible brine discharge that was discovered on July 29, 2022. The following was observed:The brine tank from where the possible discharge occurred in inspection 3400883 has since been removed, and the area has been mulched and seeded (see photos 1 and 2). The hissing sound and gas odor previously noted on the well head in inspections 3400883 and 3399998 is no longer present (see photo 4). Newly updated operator's information has also been added (see photo 3). Soil conductivity readings were taken on both sides of what once appeared to be the brine puddle. The one taken on the side closest to the well at the former location of the brine tank read, .49 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken on the side farthest away from the well read .44 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). An additional reading was taken on the side closest to the well at the former brine tank location, but approximately 6 inches of soil was dug before the reading was taken. It read .38 Micro Siemens. A background reading was taken 50 feet west of the well which read .24 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). Overall, the conductivity of the soil at the site of the possible brine release appears to now be comparable to the surrounding soil.Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of August 26, 2022. However, outstanding violations issued during inspection record 3400883 shall remain open since no NOV response or any of the information requested has been received from the operator.

Comments: On Thursday, 9/18/2025, I conducted an inspection of the Oil and Gas Management, Inc. Brown 2 well, permit number 005-29119, due to complaint received 9/16/2025 (CTS #392326). The site is located in the woods off of Chestnut Road in Parks township, Armstrong county. The complaint was submitted as a result of a spill on the site. The spill appears to be used motor oil and I estimated that more than 25 gallons was spilled. This was due to containers (2 - 5 gallon buckets and a 55 gallon drum) and refuse (used oil filter) observed in the immediate area of the spill (see pictures 3, 4, and 5). The operator did not report the spill and it appears that the operator has not visited the site recently. The well was shut in on the day of the inspection, but the operator did report a non-averaged production of 729.0 mcf for the 2024 production (365 days producing, as per OGRE). The well appeared to be disconnected from the compressor (see picture 9) and the compressor does not appear to be functional at this time (no motor, see picture 8). It needs to be noted that the production chart is dated 4-2-23 (see picture 3). The site access road is also in terrible condition. The E and S BMP's have not been maintained and there are multiple areas that are deeply rutted and have significant accelerated erosion.As a result of the site conditions, the operator is being cited for violations to 25 PA Code 78.53, 102.22(a), 102.4(b)(1), 78.57(a), 78.66(b), and CSL 402(b)

Upon arrival to the site, staff from Pennhills were actively working to remediate the issue. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/30/2025 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/30/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8239850
Permit API: 081-21995
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/30/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite on 6/30/25 in response to a reported release of at least 5 gallons of produced fluid. The release occurred near the evaporator units on the eastern side of the pad and may have been the result of a faulty inlet valve on the evaporators. Tobias Machine and Welding, Penn E and R, and Rick Hall (EQT) were onsite to screen and assess the extent of the release. There were two stains visible on the pad (Photos 1 and 2). The larger stain was approximately 13' by 6' and the smaller stain was approximately 4' by 1'. There was no visible fluid off the pad surface but soil conductivity readings were taken. The soil below the staining between the toe of the pad slope and about halfway to the treeline (Photos 3, 4, and 5) had conductivities over 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). Closer to the trees the soil conductivity dropped to around 2.2 mS/cm. Inside the woods the conductivity ranged between 0.05 mS/cm to 0.21 mS/cm.I returned on 7/2/25 to check on the progress of the remediation. The impacted area had been scraped (Photos 6, 7, and 8). Soil conductivity was again checked. Conductivities outside the scraped area ranged from 0.20 mS/cm to 0.40 mS/cm. There were a few localized areas within the work area that ranged between 1.74 mS/cm and 3.17 mS/cm. These readings were generally shallow and appeared where there were scrape marks from the excavation. Tobias was going to continue removing soil from these areas as they were finishing the bulk of the remediation. The excavated area was roughly 50' from the pad to the treeline and about 20' to 30' across.During a phone call with Rick Hall (EQT) on 7/3/25, it was determined that the remediated area had been backfilled and stabilized. There were 7 dumpsters of impacted soil that were in the process of being disposed of. EQT also indicated that remediation under Act 2 would be pursued and Penn E and R already collected the necessary confirmation samples.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). The violations may be closed after the completion of Act 2 remediation.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 8195329
Permit API: 015-21313
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/22/2024
Comments: Weather was 74¿¿ and cloudy. There were no Chesapeake representatives on location at time of inspection. Well appeared to be capable of production. Well had digital pressure monitoring equipment attached reading 1 PSI on the well head and -3 PSI on the production casing. Well had 2 annulus vents plumbed to the production tank with digital pressure monitoring equipment attached. The surface casing (13 3/8") X intermediate casing (9 5/8") annulus vent read 0 PSI and the intermediate casing (9 5/8") X production casing (5 1/2") annulus vent read 5 PSI. During the inspection, the 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" annulus vent was opened to atmosphere and 78% LEL and 6% Methane/Volume was detected. Creston arrived onsite and detected combustible gas (e.g., bubbling) in the cellar and on the 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" annulus vent. No gas was observed leaking from the wellhead during the inspection. In an email dated 7/25/2024, Chesapeake provided the following information after further evaluating the stray gas observed during the inspection: "As per our conversation, the well head crew observed minimal, intermittent bubbles in cellar. Bubbling was not confined to one area and appeared to be coming from various spots. GM site truck pulled water and FMC wellhead techs moved in to inspect wellhead components and piping for leaks. NO GAS leaks detected Pressure test 5-1/2"x 9-5/8" hanger seals to 1500 psi- GOOD test Pressure test 9-5/8"x13-3/8" hanger seals to 1500 psi- GOOD test They secured well head. LEL 50%- 90% detected in the 13-3/8" vent line." The Department's investigation of the Hopson 5H well found that combustible gas is currently venting outside of the surface casing string. This is a violation of the Department's regulations relating to Cement Standards, 25 Pa. Code ¿¿78a.85(a)(5), which provides: "When cementing surface casing or coal protective casing, the operator shall use cement that meets or exceeds the ASTM International C 150, Type I, II, or III Standard or API Specification 10. The cement must also: (5) Prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used." The Department’s investigation of the Hopson 5H well also detected the presence of combustible gas at the 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" annulus vent. This is a violation of the Department’s regulations relating to Defective Cement, 25 Pa. Code ¿¿78a.86, which provides "In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under ¿¿ 78.91 – 78.98 (related to plugging)." Please provide a written response detailing how Chesapeake intends to comply with this regulation, including information regarding the suspected source of stray gas, by 8/23/2024.

Comments: This inspection was performed in response to a report, by the Operator, of a small release of crude oil along Irvine Run, in Brokenstraw Township, Warren County, PA. This is the second release to have occurred in association with this well this year. Please reference inspection ID#: 2870841. I was contacted by Rick Engelbert with Irvine Run Resources on September 13, 2019 to report the release of an unknown volume of crude oil to the ground along Irvine Run. The spill was reported to have been contained and was actively being cleaned up. A site visit was arranged for September 16, 2019. Legree 30, (37-123-26419): I met with Rick Engelbert on site at approximately 10:30 on September 16, 2019 to conduct an site investigation. Rick indicated that the well was pumped on August 31, 2019. A strong odor was noticed near the well on September 1st. A small amount of oil was found to have been seeping from the ground surface at the base of a hill side some ways below the well location;(At a similar elevation as the spill that occurred in April but further down on Irvine Run). A syphon dam was constructed below the area that was seeping oil. Absorbent materials were applied periodically to absorb the oil. A boom and some straw bails were placed in the stream channel of Irvine Run as a precautionary measure. Very little oil was believed to have made it into the stream. A leak test was performed on the buried lead line system that services the well. A small hole was found in a portion of the line near the well. The excavation exposing the line was still open while I was on site. All of the contaminated soil appeared to have been removed from the hole. Similar to the excavation created to expose the last leak associated with this well, the soil that was excavated didn't seem to have much oil contamination. Heavy rain in the last week apparently caused the volume of oil draining from the seep to increase. It was at this point that Rick contacted me to report the spill. Approximately ten gallons of oil is reported to have been gather up. I noticed a slight emulsion on the surface of the water behind the syphon dam while I was on site. The spill appears to be getting managed appropriately at this point. The operator indicated the absorbent materials will continue to be changed as needed. It has been advised to the operator that recoverable waste materials, including the contaminated soil that was excavated around the leak, be collected and disposed of at a land fill. A receipt of disposal should be sent to the Warren District Office upon disposal. The clean up progress will continue to be monitored with future inspections.

The above violations will be resolved upon submission of a waste manifest to the Department for the excavated material and inspection of the site.

Violation ID: 853324
Permit API: 117-21998
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-06-21
Comments: Results from sample IDs 0718-020 through 022, collected on 5/13/19 as documented in inspection report 2879933, were received from the lab on 6/21/19. At the time of inspection, WQS Sara Metz observed water discharging from the pad into the infiltration basin. Conductivity of the discharge ranged from 0.999 to 1.669 mS/cm, and conductivity in the basin where the discharge was entering was 1.493 mS/cm. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in sample 0718-020, collected from the infiltration basin, indicate that the discharge was a pollutional substance. The discharge of a pollutional substance to the infiltration basin, considered Waters of the Commonwealth, is a violation of Section 401 of the Clean Streams Law. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in sample 0718-021, collected from a high-conductivity puddle (18.75 mS/cm) on the pad near a crushed containment berm, also indicate a release of a pollutional substance to the pad surface (as compared to sample 0718-022 collected from an area of the pad containing water with conductivity under 1 mS/cm). It is unclear whether this affected area is separate from or related to the affected area described in a previous Notice of Violation issued on 6/10/19 with inspection report 2890742. Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. Conductivity readings were taken in the vegetation that is now impacted by sediment laden waters and they are as follows: 0.410 mS in the sediment laden puddle created from the flow going off the shoulder of the road, 0.464 mS in the vegetation adjacent to where the previous puddle reading was taken, 0.502 mS in some vegetation that is further in the intermittent tributary, and lastly 0.157 mS upslope of the Act 9 sign as a background reading. Though these readings subjugate that freshwater is being released, it is evident that sediment is still entering Waters of the Commonwealth. While onsite, the Department notified John Hulsey about the sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth and advised them to promptly cease all water release dust suppression activities on the access road.The Department recommends the Operator re-evaluate their dust suppression methods or implement measures to prevent sediment laden water from entering the intermittent unnamed tributary to Miller's Run.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the discharge of sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth.

Violation ID: 916953
Permit API: 117-22080
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/12/2021
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted after the operator reported a release of an estimated 20 gallons of produced water to the pad surface. The operator stated in the notification that a stain was observed on the pad surface on 5/11/21 in a load off area in front of a battery of tanks. This led to the discovery of high conductivity fluid on the pad in this area. The initial electrical conductivity readings of the fluid on the pad were between 15 to 20 mS/cm according to the operator's notification. I met with Matt Tusing of Penn E&R upon arriving on location. The area in front of a frac tank battery where the release occurred was taped off. The area has been excavated but not yet backfilled. No fluid was present in this area or in the adjacent secondary containment. No puddles were observed in other areas on the pad. The water in the stormwater controls adjacent to the pad had electrical conductivity readings of less than 1000 uS/cm. Matt Tusing said that the pad surface had soil electrical conductivity readings of less than 2000 uS/cm after excavating the area of the release. He said that approximately half of a half-round roll-off box was filled with the excavated material. The approximate area of the pad excavated was 45 ft by 45 ft. He also said that the secondary containment for the tanks was pulled back and the EC of the soil there was lower which led them to believe that the produced water did not get under the tanks. No evidence of remaining produced water was observed on the pad. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8164247
Permit API: 081-21912
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/02/2023
Comments: On November 2, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Pad D. Kirby Steck from Range Resources reported a spill of approximately 3.5 barrels of production fluid. The spill occurred when a water hauling truck operator forgot to close a valve on the production fluid tanks after removing the production fluid from the tank causing the production fluid to spill on the well pad surface. The production fluid was spilled on the south corner of the well pad at approximate coordinates 41.4837421, -77.1143370. Range Resources contractors onsite immediately began vacuuming the fluid up off the well pad surface. Range Resources delineated the area of impact and contractors began excavating the area of impact. The excavation area was about eighty feet by thirty feet with a depth of about six inches. The impacted soil was placed on containment and Range Resources is awaiting roll off dumpsters to arrive. The excavation of the area had been completed prior to DEP's arrival onsite. DEP screened the area of the reported spill with a soil conductivity meter and conductivity levels were not found above 500 uS/cm. The DEP observed the discharge area of a nearby sump for the pad and screened the discharge area with a soil conductivity meter. The discharge area did not have a conductivity measurement over 200 uS/cm. DEP spoke with Range Resources Irv Gleason and Kirby Steck. Mr. Steck said Moody and Associates are planning to collect Act 2 confirmatory samples on November 3, 2023. Due to the spill of production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301 have been noted.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: JKLM ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/28/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8181243
Permit API: 105-21857
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Summit Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/28/2024
Comments: On 03/28/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an inspection of JKLM Energy LLC's Sweden Valley 101 multi-well pad located in Summit Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1150 hours, weather was 40F and partly cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).There was standing water on the pad surface which field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of approximately 199 - 226us/cm.There are 3 wells tagged with American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers and capable of producing and located onsite (photos #2 and 3). 3 gas processing units (GPUs) stationed in a secondary containment structure are also located onsite (photo #4). The GPU containment structure contained greater than 10% standing water which field measured for EC at ~136.6us/cm. There is evidence of damage to the GPU secondary containment structure (photos #5 and 6). There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #7); the containment structure contained standing water which field measured for EC at ~10.1 us/cm. The brine pump secondary containment structure contained water which field measured for EC at ~13.66mS/cm (photos #8 and 9).A dehydrator is located onsite and associated chemicals are stationed in secondary containment (photo #10). A compressor unit and compressor waste fluids tank is located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #11). Water in the compressor fluids unit had a visible sheen and field measured for EC at ~36.6us/cm; the containment lining shows signs of damage (photos #12 and 13). The compressor waste oil storage tank is stationed in secondary containment and holding water with a sheen on it (photos #14 and 15). Oil was noted leaking from the compressor oil tank pipe fittings and staining was visible on the ground (photos #16 - 18). The affected area was approximately 10ft x 2ft, I excavated approximately 6in deep and still noted staining (photo #18). I contacted a representative from JKLM who notified the DEP spill reporting hotline of the incident and dispatched personnel to excavate and remediate the affected area immediately.
